Grimmauld Place KitchenHarry Potter and the Order of the PhoenixThe Ministry lies. The snacks don't.Every recipe serves 4.
    To StartMainsSomething SweetTo Drink
    To StartFred and George's fireworks popcornPopcorn and popping candy. The twins' fireworks crash the examsHow to make it100g popping corn1 tbsp vegetable oil60g butter, melted3 tbsp coloured sprinkles2 packets of popping candyHeat the oil in a large lidded pot and pop the corn.Toss with the melted butter and sprinkles.Scatter popping candy over just before serving so it crackles.Hog's Head pork and sage sausage rollsMince, onion and herbs in puff pastry, baked golden, with English mustard, dusty village pub styleHow to make itNot on tonight's cookSausage rolls of pork, onion and sage in puff pastry, baked at 200°C for 25 minutes, with English mustard, like a dusty village pub.Mix 500g pork mince with 1 grated onion, 1 tbsp chopped sage, 40g breadcrumbs, 1 tsp salt and plenty of pepper.Halve 2 sheets puff pastry lengthways.Lay a log of the filling down each strip, roll up and seal the seam with beaten egg.Cut each log into 4, brush with egg and score the tops.Bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until puffed and golden.Serve hot with English mustard and tomato chutney.MainsGrimmauld Place steak and kidney pieChuck steak and lamb kidney in rich gravy under puff pastryHow to make it800g chuck steak, diced200g lamb kidneys, trimmed and chopped2 tbsp olive oil1 onion, diced2 tbsp plain flour500ml beef stock2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce1 sheet puff pastry, thawed1 egg, beatenTrim and chop the steak and kidneys.Brown the meat in the olive oil in batches.Soften the onion.Stir in the flour, stock and Worcestershire sauce.Simmer until thick and tender.Spoon into a pie dish, cool slightly and cover with the pastry.Brush with egg and bake at 200°C.Great Hall thyme roast chicken and gravyDinner under the floating candles in the Great HallHow to make itNot on tonight's cookChicken rubbed with butter and thyme, roasted at 200°C for 75 minutes, with crispy roast potatoes, peas and gravy from the pan.Rub a 1.8kg chicken with 40g soft butter, salt and thyme leaves and roast at 200°C for 75 minutes.Parboil 1kg halved potatoes for 8 minutes, rough them up in the colander and roast in hot oil alongside the chicken for 50 minutes, turning once.Rest the chicken 10 minutes.Stir 1 tbsp flour into the pan juices, whisk in 300ml chicken stock and simmer until thick.Serve with buttered peas and the gravy.Something SweetTreacle tartGolden syrup and lemon. Patronus practice afterHow to make it2 sheets of shortcrust pastry, thawed400g golden syrup100g fresh breadcrumbs1 lemon300ml thickened creamLine a tart tin with the pastry.Blind bake the case.Warm the golden syrup with the breadcrumbs and lemon zest and juice.Pour into the case.Bake at 180°C until just set.Cool slightly.Serve warm slices with a pour of cream.Umbridge's pink cupcakesVanilla cupcakes, pink buttercream, kitten plates.How to make it125g butter, softened150g caster sugar2 eggs200g self-raising flour125ml milk125g butter for icing, softened250g icing sugar1 tsp pink food colouring12 sugar flowers12 cupcake casesBeat the cake butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs.Fold in the flour and milk.Spoon into cupcake cases.Bake at 175°C.Cool completely.Beat the icing butter, icing sugar and pink colouring.Pipe on top and finish each with a sugar flower.To DrinkPumpkin juicePumpkin and apple. Harry sees the Thestrals, and so does LunaHow to make it300g butternut pumpkin, chopped1 L apple juice1 tbsp honey1/4 tsp ground cinnamon3 cups iceChop the pumpkin.Roast at 200°C until soft.Cool completely.Blend with the apple juice, honey and cinnamon until smooth.Strain into a jug and chill well.Pour into goblets over ice.Iced lemon barley waterLuna's pick, Quibbler held upside down.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
